terms.definition: One change you want to make. The runner gives it a permanent id (I003), and everything about it lives in delivery/intents/I003-<slug>/.
The ai-sdlc program. It owns ids, state, gates, evidence and the audit log. Studio and the agent ask it; neither writes its records directly.
A decision only a person can make (G1 to G5). The runner refuses to move an Intent past it until someone approves, and records who.
Undo an approval on the record, with a reason, so an approved artifact can change. Evidence that depended on it no longer counts until the gate is approved again.
01-brief/brief.md: the problem, the expected outcome, and how success is measured, in plain language.
One testable statement of what the system shall do (REQ-F-001) or how well (REQ-NFR-001). It lives in 02-specification/requirements.yaml.
Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax: sentence shapes such as 'When <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>' that make a requirement testable.
How one requirement is proved (AC-001). Each criterion has exactly one verification class.
How a criterion is checked. D deterministic, S statistical, J judged, N adversarial. Exactly one per criterion.
Deterministic: a command that passes or fails the same way every time. Most tests.
Statistical: run three times on a registered dataset; the median must meet the threshold and every run must stay within the tolerance band.
Judged: a calibrated model from a different family scores the output, in both orders, with agreement of at least 0.85 against human labels.
Adversarial: attacks replayed from a dataset. It passes only with zero successful attacks.
A measure from the brief (SC-001), tied to the acceptance criteria that demonstrate it.
An OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or JSON Schema file in 02-specification/contracts/. Every operation must be covered by a criterion or excluded with a reason.
02-specification/threat-model.yaml: trust boundaries, each answering all six STRIDE categories with a threat or a reason it does not apply.
Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege: the six kinds of threat a boundary must answer.
A group of Tasks (I003-P01). P00 comes first; everything after it waits for G4.
Phase P00: the thinnest slice that proves the approach end to end before the rest is built.
One unit of work an agent can finish in one focused context (I003-P00-T001). It traces to a requirement, finding or decision.
What the runner captured when it ran a Task's checks: commands, exit codes, output hashes, pinned to a git commit. Never edited by hand.
A check the implementer does not see, written from the specification. It catches work that passes the visible tests but misses the requirement.
Visible checks pass but held-out checks fail: the work was tuned to the tests rather than the requirement.
An adversarial review of the spec (before G2) or plan (before G3) by the red-team agent, from a fresh context and a different model family.
A Task is verified only when a reviewer from a different model family than the implementer approves its evidence.
The check before G5: every Task verified at one commit, evaluations current, no open critical or high finding, traceability complete.
A problem someone found (F-001), with severity and the stage it entered and was caught at. Lives in 05-verification/findings.yaml.
A finding generalised into a rule (LESSON-001). Once promoted, later Intents with the same trigger must answer it.
A promoted lesson that every later Intent with a matching trigger flag must answer in its threat model.
Facts about an Intent (multi_tenant, has_side_effect, retrieval_grounded, contains_model_behavior) that decide which standing suites and threats it inherits.
Part of the change is produced by an AI model, so it needs S, J or N evaluations and full mode, not only tests.
For small, well-understood changes: no brief or master plan required, only Class D criteria, and G2 and G3 approved together.
For new behaviour, risk, security or model output: brief, threat model when risky, evaluations, and a phased plan.
Mapping an existing codebase (/aisdlc:understand) and pinning its current behaviour (/aisdlc:baseline) before specifying a change to it.
A commit-pinned snapshot of what probes report today (BASELINE-001). A later comparison fails only on regressions.
Two active Intents change the same contract operation or declared resource. It is reported, not blocked; serialise them or co-approve with a reason.
An architecture decision recorded by the runner (I003-D001), with alternatives. An accepted decision must be implemented by a Task.
A group of Intents with ordering and roll-up reporting (PRG001). It carries no gates of its own.
The runner's requirement-quality rules (SQ001 to SQ018). Errors block entry to G2; warnings and notes inform the approver.
What a reopened G2 costs if approved: requirements and criteria that changed, and the Tasks whose evidence stops counting.
The chain requirement → criterion → Task → evidence, generated by the runner into traceability.json.

lint_rules.title: Unfinished requirement
lint_rules.explanation: A placeholder or TBD is still in the text.
lint_rules.fix: Replace it with the real value, or move the open question to the brief.

lint_rules.title: Ambiguous term
lint_rules.explanation: Words like 'fast' or 'user-friendly' cannot be tested.
lint_rules.fix: Quantify it (within 200 ms), or define it in the glossary.

lint_rules.title: Open-ended list
lint_rules.explanation: 'etc.' or 'such as' leaves the checked cases undefined.
lint_rules.fix: List every case the criterion will check.

lint_rules.title: More than one behaviour
lint_rules.explanation: Two binding clauses in one requirement cannot pass or fail separately.

lint_rules.title: Unmeasured quality requirement
lint_rules.explanation: A non-functional requirement with no measure has no target to test.
lint_rules.fix: Declare metric, target, unit and condition.

lint_rules.title: No binding modal
lint_rules.explanation: Without shall, must or will, the statement is not an obligation.

lint_rules.title: No quality category
lint_rules.explanation: The coverage report cannot place a non-functional requirement without a category.
lint_rules.fix: Add a category such as performance, security or accessibility.

lint_rules.title: No priority
lint_rules.explanation: Without must, should, could or won't, nobody knows what can be cut.

lint_rules.title: No rationale or source
lint_rules.explanation: Nobody will know later why the requirement exists.
lint_rules.fix: Add a rationale or the source it came from.

lint_rules.title: Unprotected personal data
lint_rules.explanation: Personal or confidential data is handled, but no requirement says how it is protected.
lint_rules.fix: Add a privacy, security or compliance requirement.

lint_rules.title: Prohibition tested only by Class D
lint_rules.explanation: 'Shall not' is usually an adversarial property.
lint_rules.fix: Add a Class N criterion with attack cases.

lint_rules.title: Undemonstrated success measure
lint_rules.explanation: A success criterion references no acceptance criterion.
lint_rules.fix: Link the criteria that demonstrate it.

lint_rules.title: Undeclared contract
lint_rules.explanation: A contract file is not listed under `contracts`, so nothing has to cover it.
lint_rules.fix: Declare it with its path and api.

lint_rules.title: Silent trust boundary
lint_rules.explanation: A boundary does not answer every STRIDE category.
lint_rules.fix: Name a threat, or record why the category does not apply.

lint_rules.title: Risky Intent without a threat model
lint_rules.explanation: Security, multi-tenant or side-effecting work has no threat model.
lint_rules.fix: Use full mode and write threat-model.yaml.

lint_rules.title: No manual accessibility audit
lint_rules.explanation: Automated checkers decide only a minority of WCAG success criteria.

lint_rules.title: Glossary clash
lint_rules.explanation: The spec redefines a term the repository glossary already owns.
lint_rules.fix: Use the shared definition, or ask its owner to change it.

lint_rules.title: Contract without an api identity
lint_rules.explanation: Cross-Intent contention and breaking-change checks cannot see it.

# Intent Brief: I001 — Customer export API

## Problem

Finance reconciles the ledger monthly by asking support to run SQL against production.
It takes two days, and last quarter a query exported another region's customers.

## Expected outcome

An administrator requests a CSV export of their own customers and downloads it without
involving support.

## Success measures

- 100% of monthly reconciliation exports self-served by administrators (baseline: 0%).
- An export of 100 000 customers completes within 30 seconds at p95.

## Out of scope

- XLSX format (finance has not confirmed it).

# Intent Brief: I001 — Customer export API

## Problem

Finance reconciles the ledger monthly by asking support to run SQL against production.
It takes two days, and last quarter a query exported another region's customers.

## Expected outcome

An administrator requests a CSV export of their own customers and downloads it without
involving support.

## Success measures

- 100% of monthly reconciliation exports self-served by administrators (baseline: 0%).
- An export of 100 000 customers completes within 30 seconds at p95.

## Out of scope

- XLSX format (finance has not confirmed it).

# Findings for one Intent: delivery/intents/<Ixxx>-<slug>/05-verification/findings.yaml
# Validated against schemas/finding.schema.json by `ai-sdlc validate-intent` and at convergence.
# Stages are numbered 0 Register, 1 Frame, 2 Specify, 3 Plan, 4 Build, 5 Converge, 6 Close.
# A critical or high finding cannot be closed until a blocking lesson covers it (`lesson_ref`).
findings:
  - id: F-001                          # F-001, F-002, ... never reuse one
    severity: high                     # critical | high | medium | low
    status: open                       # open | resolved | accepted | escalated
    source: "{{WHO_OR_WHAT_FOUND_IT}}" # e.g. "G2 pre-gate review PR-1", "I003-P00-T001 verifier"
    requirement: "{{REQUIREMENT_ID}}"  # optional: the requirement it concerns

    impact: "{{WHAT_HAPPENS_IF_IT_SHIPS}}"
    recommended_action: "{{WHAT_TO_DO}}"

    detected_stage: 2                  # the stage it was caught; the loop metrics measure the gap
